name: langgraph-server
notes: Deliberately a separate subject from the `langgraph` library: this one is the running server measured end to end, that one is the persistence model measured in isolation. Merging them would blur which was which.
Self-hostable dev server with the Postgres checkpointer. The interesting result is not raw latency but write amplification: a full checkpoint per super-step against Brain's append.
Run the write-cost-against-turn-index arm here, not a single-figure comparison.

Pinned to langgraph-api 0.13.0, released 2026-08-21, the latest at survey time. Run at documented defaults: `langgraph dev` with the in-memory checkpointer unless the Postgres arm is the one being measured.

The graph the server runs is ours (subjects/langgraph-server/graph/bench_graph.py): one node that calls the model and appends the reply, the smallest fair analogue of Brain's agentloop. Any published number has to say we wrote it.
The persistence figure from `langgraph dev` is against the in-memory checkpointer and must not be charted against Brain's durable log. Run the Postgres checkpointer arm for that comparison.

cold_start.definition: process launch on a fresh data directory until the first turn is served; one-time installation untimed

recovery.definition: kill -9 after 50 turns, relaunch on the same data, until the same session serves a turn whose model request carries its history

create.definition: thread create until it will accept input

ttfb.definition: run submitted until the first model output byte on the run's own SSE response; scripted provider. Unlike Brain's, the stream is opened by submitting the run rather than before it, so the subscribe cost is inside this number by construction

round_trip.definition: input submitted until the run completes

resident.definition: private memory across the server tree, excluding Postgres, held minus post-discard, per thread

persistence.definition: bytes on disk in the server's data directory after N turns of one thread, sampled per turn. MEASURED AGAINST THE IN-MEMORY CHECKPOINTER that `langgraph dev` runs, which is not a durable store: this number is not comparable to a subject that writes every turn to disk, and the Postgres arm has to be run separately before any persistence comparison is published
